jsonLd.headline: Pokemon TCG Card Value Scanner: How to Check What Your Cards Are Worth
jsonLd.description: A complete guide to using a Pokemon TCG card value scanner — how AI card recognition works, step-by-step scanning tips, and how to get accurate prices for your collection.

mainEntity.name: What is the best Pokemon TCG card value scanner app?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best card scanner apps combine AI-based visual recognition with live market data from TCGPlayer and Cardmarket. Look for apps that update prices in real-time, support multiple card sets, and let you save your scans to a personal collection.

mainEntity.name: How accurate are Pokemon card scanning apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Modern AI-based scanners are highly accurate for identifying cards from major sets — typically above 95% for clean, well-lit cards. Accuracy drops for cards with heavy wear, foil glare, or very old sets with limited training data.

mainEntity.name: Can I scan Pokemon cards that are in sleeves or binders?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, most scanner apps handle cards in protective sleeves, though matte sleeves produce better results than glossy ones which can create glare. Scanning through binder pockets works but may slightly reduce recognition accuracy.

mainEntity.name: How often do Pokemon card prices change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pokemon card prices fluctuate constantly — sometimes daily for popular cards. New set releases, tournament results, social media attention, and influencer pulls can cause rapid price swings. Always check current prices before buying or selling.

mainEntity.name: Are old Pokemon cards worth anything?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many older Pokemon cards — particularly Base Set holographics, first editions, and shadowless variants — are worth significant amounts. A Base Set Charizard in Near Mint condition can sell for hundreds to thousands of dollars. Always scan or look up older cards before assuming they have no value.
